 Oct. 30, 2026, 7:21 PM UTC ;  Updated: Oct. 30, 2026, 8:38 PM UTC Tiana Headley Reporter The Education Department has failed to process the “buyback” applications of nearly 90,000 borrowers, a new complaint says. Photographer: JEFF PACHOUD/AFP via Getty Images The American Federation of Teachers and student loan borrowers have sued the Education Department for its alleged mismanagement of the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program.
 The lawsuit claims the second Trump administration has operated the program, which cancels student loan debt for government and nonprofit workers after 120 payments, in ways that have denied or stalled loan forgiveness those borrowers were promised.
 “The Department’s actions more than break the promise of PSLF — they create a financial and emotional burden for public service workers,” AFT and the borrowers, who are seeking class action status, said in their Friday complaint filed ...
